identityStatus: Exact Q648226 castle relation with physical outline and courtyard inner ring. Other castle parts,defense walls,coast and access paths are separately attributed nearby features.

portal.basis: Mapped old-gate route defines the signed passage axis. Original34m cutting envelope extends through both exterior and courtyard walls; the mapped line ends inside the thick gate tower. Width,height and arch remain photographic estimates.

bridge.basis: Mapped western timber access bridge; width/deck/pier/rail dimensions estimated.

well.basis: Mapped small courtyard roof interpreted as the Renaissance well canopy from SFV aerial. Own simplified columns/basin/entablature; no inscription/sculpture reproduction.

controls.roofWingBasis: Outer eaves follow the exact mapped palace walls between the separately modeled corner towers; inner eaves follow the exact mapped courtyard. Four estimated ridge segments join matching wing corners. This replaces the inset four-corner roof envelope that left broad mapped walls unroofed. Protruding Renaissance gables retain their separate cross roofs; roof heights and profiles remain photographic estimates.

nativeAxes.front: Mapped western bridge and old Kuretornet entrance, baked into East/South coordinates
nativeAxes.origin: Exact-QID footprint map anchor; model ground attachment Y4.2 is an original provisional castle-platform estimate. Outer defenses descend toY0.3.

reconstruction.scope: Present-day exterior: hollow courtyard ring with four gabled wings,four differentiated copper tower caps,square Kuretornet and physical old-gate passage,selected white Renaissance gables,original well canopy,outer grass defenses and four separately mapped cannon towers,timber approach bridge and access route.
reconstruction.basis: Own mapped coordinates plus original interpretation of operator/SFV primary history and aerial/moat photographs. No traced printed drawing,downloaded mesh or photo texture.
reconstruction.referenceState: Current-state approximation; vertical heights,roof profiles,apertures,outer banks and modern fixtures remain estimates.
